title: The Best Early Black Friday Deals on Laptops I’ve Tested Myself
gist: Wired's laptop reviewer flags early Black Friday laptop discounts: Apple's MacBook Neo gets its first notable cut to $649 after seven months, while Snapdragon-based Windows machines (Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x, HP OmniBook 5, 2024 Surface Laptop) are discounted to $750–$900. The piece implicitly shows the MacBook Neo setting the price anchor that entry-level Windows laptops are now judged against.

insights.claim: Apple's MacBook Neo, out for seven months, received its first meaningful price cut during early Black Friday sales, dropping $50 to $649 at Amazon, Best Buy and Target.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Apple's reluctance to discount its cheapest laptop signals pricing discipline; a holiday cut is a watch-point for Mac unit demand at the low end.
insights.quote: Apple hasn't been eager to give much in the way of price cuts—despite the laptop having been out for seven months
insights.locator: The Biggest MacBook Neo Discount Ever

insights.claim: Wired's reviewer rates the $649 MacBook Neo as an affordable laptop that feels premium (metal chassis, quality display), with 8 GB of RAM as its main limitation.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: A sub-$700 Mac with premium build pressures Windows OEMs competing in the entry-level segment.
insights.locator: The Biggest MacBook Neo Discount Ever

insights.claim: At $649, the MacBook Neo makes an entry-level Windows laptop such as the HP OmniBook 5 on sale for $750 look poorly positioned, in the reviewer's view, unless its 16 GB of RAM is the deciding factor.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Cheap Macs compress the price/spec room for Windows OEMs like HP, forcing deeper discounts or higher-RAM configurations.
insights.quote: being $100 more than the MacBook Neo doesn't seems like a great position to be in for an entry-level Windows laptop

insights.claim: The Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x, a 15-inch OLED laptop with 16 GB of RAM, 512 GB storage and next-generation Snapdragon chips, sells for about $900 and is described as a rare sub-$1,000 laptop without major compromises.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Qualcomm Snapdragon Windows PCs are reaching compelling price/performance at sub-$1,000, a data point for Arm PC adoption.
insights.quote: you'll be hard-pressed to find a laptop for under $1,000 that doesn't have any major compromises

insights.claim: Microsoft's 2024 Surface Laptop 13.8-inch (7th Edition) is discounted 34% to $900 on Amazon, while the newer Snapdragon X2 Plus/Elite version remains quite expensive according to the reviewer.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Steep discounting of two-year-old Surface stock alongside pricey new X2 models shows how Microsoft is clearing older Arm inventory.

insights.claim: The HP OmniBook 5 14-inch, with OLED display, thin chassis, 16 GB RAM and a Snapdragon X chip delivering strong battery life, is discounted 35% to $750 at HP, though its touchpad is criticized as clumsy.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Deep discounts on Snapdragon X laptops suggest OEMs are using price to move Arm Windows inventory.
